Identity (name/element/affinity) stays in the EchoRosterCatalog CODE table; ONLY the numbers live here. OWNER RULING 2026-08-02 (F8 on the Echo card, 'should be +5% not 55%'): the per-echo readout showed +55% because the card prints base+match (0.15 + 0.40). Rescaled so a MATCHED echo at Lv 1 reads +5% (base 0.02 + match 0.03) and an UNMATCHED one reads +2% -- matching still pays 2.5x, so the affinity choice still means something. perLevelBonus dropped 0.05 -> 0.01 in the same breath: at the old value one level-up would have outweighed the entire matched bonus, which would have made the affinity pick cosmetic. Lv 8 matched now reads +12%. NOTE FOR THE OWNER: the synergy/set knobs below were NOT rescaled -- crossBonuses 0.10 each, hiddenTriSynergyBonus 0.25 and sixSetBonusGlobalHarvest 0.20 are now LARGE relative to a 0.05 per-echo contribution, so team composition now dominates individual assignment. That may be exactly what you want (it rewards collecting the set); say the word if they should scale down too. WO-830 history: preferredLaneMatchBonus was lowered 0.75 -> 0.40 for the all-matched reality (all 6 Echoes now prefer Harvest and the player picks each resource); crossBonuses are the 3 DISCLOSED pair synergies (both members owned + both harvesting their own affinity resource); hiddenTriSynergyBonus is the UNDISCLOSED bonus when all 3 pairs run at once -- applied to income only, NEVER shown in any readout. perEchoBaseRate doubles as the DumpSilos split weight per assigned resource: Bran+Maren (0.45 each) are the two Crystals harvesters and their COMBINED 0.90 stays below every other single affinity rate (food/gold 1.0, wood 1.1, iron 1.15) so crystals remain the slowest faucet (monetization guard, WO-830 Sec.3b). WO-1108 (2026-08-16, D3): repairFractionPerHour moved OUT of code (it was a hidden default of 2.0 in EchoBalanceCatalog.cs, never authored here) and re-tuned to 0.35, because WO-1108 made repair PASSIVE -- EchoBonusCalculator.RepairFractionsPerSecond dropped its lane filter and now sums EVERY OWNED Echo instead of only the ones assigned to a repair task. ARITHMETIC: old felt rate = ONE repair-assigned Lv1 Echo = 2.0 x (1 + baseContributionPerEcho 0.02) = 2.04 structure-fractions/hour. Leaving the knob at 2.0 would give a full 6-Echo roster 6 x 2.04 = 12.24/h, a silent 6x buff. Anchoring the FULL roster at parity gives 2.04 / 6 = 0.34; rounded to 0.35 the 6-Echo aggregate is 6 x 0.35 x 1.02 = 2.14/h (+5% vs the old felt rate). Early game is intentionally slower per-Echo (1 Echo = 0.357/h) because passive repair is now FREE -- it no longer costs the Echo its harvest assignment, so the per-Echo rate had to come down. OWNER: this is the tuning dial -- raise it if mending feels too slow to notice; each +0.1 adds ~0.61/h at a full roster. Repair still SPENDS materials (F8-42 canon), so the knob only sets pace, never cost. Keep EchoBalanceData.RepairFractionPerHour's code default in step with this value. WO-1474 (2026-09-06): harvestRatePerHour was ADDED -- the three workforce rates (common 3600 / gold 900 / crystals 4) were private consts in EchoBonusCalculator.cs and therefore out of reach of the WO-1331 remote seam; they are authored here at the SAME values, so the move alone changes no number. In the same pass perEchoBaseRate finally became LIVE: HarvestTargetWeights now multiplies each Echo's per-hour rate by BaseRateFor(id) -- it resolved the roster entry and then discarded it before today -- so the sentence above about perEchoBaseRate doubling as the DumpSilos split weight is now TRUE rather than aspirational. EFFECT ON THE LIVE SPLIT at an all-matched roster: Wood x1.1 (echo-verdant-stag), Iron x1.15 (echo-stonewarden-bear), Crystals x0.45 (echo-ember-phoenix); Food and both Gold Echoes are authored at 1.0 and do not move. STALE ABOVE: the 'Bran+Maren (0.45 each) are the two Crystals harvesters' sentence does not match the authored rows -- only echo-ember-phoenix is 0.45, and echo-stormcoil-serpent is a GOLD Echo at 1.0.",

FORMULA: materialBase = clamp(round(goldBase * goldToMaterialMultiplier * perMaterialMultiplier[m]), materialFloorPerKill, materialCapPerKill), then variance-rolled through the ONE authority EnemyDef.RollReward with the enemy's own rewardVariance so all four materials feel like one drop. goldBase is the SAME resolved base the WO-432/433 gold grant uses (EnemyDef.CoinReward, else max(4, xpReward*0.4)) so every enemy pays and the payout scales with difficulty. WHY 1.1: measured from enemies.json (19 rows, 2026-08-26) gold base is min 3 / median 18 / mean 31.1 / max 120; 1.1 puts the MEDIAN enemy (troll-mage, gold 18) at 20 -- the ruled number -- while preserving scale-with-difficulty. A FLAT 20 was considered and REJECTED: it makes farming the weakest enemy optimal. A 0.25 constant was discussed earlier and is SUPERSEDED (it was agreed on a misread of per-WAVE vs per-KILL and pays ~10x under intent). "notes": "Build-mode structure catalog  -  DATA-DRIVEN. Add a row here (+ keep the Resources/Data/Canonical copy byte-equal) and it flows into CatalogRegistry at startup via CatalogBootstrap. 'type' / 'mustSitOn' / 'navSurface' / 'element' are enum NAMES (StringEnumConverter). 'visualPrefabPath' is a Resources-relative path (LogWarning-safe on miss per CLAUDE.md §4). 'behaviorId' is resolved to a Village component by StructureFactory.AttachBehavior  -  only DefenseTower / WallSegment / CrystalMine / Gate are wired; null = inert decoration. S4: 'repo.cost' is the multi-resource build cost (wood/food/iron/crystals); it is charged + refunded through the persisted ResourceLedger (EconomyService). When 'cost' is omitted / all-zero, placement falls back to charging 'buildCost' Crystals (back-compat). S5 (the CoC upgrade sink): 'repo.maxLevel' (default 1 = not upgradeable; ceiling = RepoProps.MaxStructureLevel, raised 3 -> 6 by WO-966 for the storage containers; the StructureTierVisual accent ladder still tops out at 3, which is cosmetic only) is the highest level the UPGRADE verb can reach; 'repo.upgradeCost' is an optional per-step multi-resource table indexed by the level being upgraded TO minus 2 (entry [0] = L1->L2, [1] = L2->L3, ... [4] = L5->L6). When 'upgradeCost' is omitted, the upgrade cost falls back to the build 'cost' scaled by the level being left (L1->L2 = 1x, L2->L3 = 2x) -- a fallback that goes badly wrong on a long ladder, which is why the six-level containers author the table explicitly. StructureTierVisual steps the look (scale + bronze/silver/gold accent); DefenseTower range/damage and WallSegment toughness step the stats. v5 (StructureSingleton v2, owner only-ever-one ruling): 'repo.bakedTwins' lists the legacy baked scene-root GameObject names that REPRESENT a singleton row (twin standdown/resurface + IsBuilt, enforced generically by StructureSingleton with zero per-row code); null/absent = none; only meaningful with 'repo.singleton': true.",

"_authoringNotes": "WORK_ORDER_738 + WORK_ORDER_830 -- Echo specialization + affinity/synergy balance. Tunable knobs the owner re-tunes in playtest with NO recompile [WO-1331 CORRECTION, 2026-09-02 -- READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE PHRASE ABOVE: 'no recompile' has NEVER meant 'no rebuild'. Assets/Resources IS COMPILED INTO THE PLAYER and LocalJsonCatalogSource resolves Resources FIRST on every platform, so editing this file still costs a full Unity player build (~10 min APK / ~30 min WebGL) before it reaches a device -- and editing the StreamingAssets twin alone changes nothing at all. That is the axis the owner actually cares about, and it is why every past 'move the numbers into JSON' fix did not solve what she was asking for. WO-1331 landed the remote catalog seam (CanonicalJson.Source / RemoteCatalogOverrides) that finally makes a rebuild-free retune possible; it ships FLAG-GATED AND OFF (ff.catalogremote). THIS FILE IS ON THE WO-1331 REMOTE ALLOWLIST, so once the seam is armed and a row exists it can be retuned without any build. See docs/reference/TUNABLE_LEVER_INVENTORY.md section 2.] (loaded via CanonicalJson; the Resources copy wins, StreamingAssets is the desktop source -- keep the two byte-identical). Identity (name/element/affinity) stays in the EchoRosterCatalog CODE table; ONLY the numbers live here. OWNER RULING 2026-08-02 (F8 on the Echo card, 'should be +5% not 55%'): the per-echo readout showed +55% because the card prints base+match (0.15 + 0.40). Rescaled so a MATCHED echo at Lv 1 reads +5% (base 0.02 + match 0.03) and an UNMATCHED one reads +2% -- matching still pays 2.5x, so the affinity choice still means something. perLevelBonus dropped 0.05 -> 0.01 in the same breath: at the old value one level-up would have outweighed the entire matched bonus, which would have made the affinity pick cosmetic. Lv 8 matched now reads +12%. NOTE FOR THE OWNER: the synergy/set knobs below were NOT rescaled -- crossBonuses 0.10 each, hiddenTriSynergyBonus 0.25 and sixSetBonusGlobalHarvest 0.20 are now LARGE relative to a 0.05 per-echo contribution, so team composition now dominates individual assignment. That may be exactly what you want (it rewards collecting the set); say the word if they should scale down too. WO-830 history: preferredLaneMatchBonus was lowered 0.75 -> 0.40 for the all-matched reality (all 6 Echoes now prefer Harvest and the player picks each resource); crossBonuses are the 3 DISCLOSED pair synergies (both members owned + both harvesting their own affinity resource); hiddenTriSynergyBonus is the UNDISCLOSED bonus when all 3 pairs run at once -- applied to income only, NEVER shown in any readout. perEchoBaseRate doubles as the DumpSilos split weight per assigned resource: Bran+Maren (0.45 each) are the two Crystals harvesters and their COMBINED 0.90 stays below every other single affinity rate (food/gold 1.0, wood 1.1, iron 1.15) so crystals remain the slowest faucet (monetization guard, WO-830 Sec.3b). WO-1108 (2026-08-16, D3): repairFractionPerHour moved OUT of code (it was a hidden default of 2.0 in EchoBalanceCatalog.cs, never authored here) and re-tuned to 0.35, because WO-1108 made repair PASSIVE -- EchoBonusCalculator.RepairFractionsPerSecond dropped its lane filter and now sums EVERY OWNED Echo instead of only the ones assigned to a repair task. ARITHMETIC: old felt rate = ONE repair-assigned Lv1 Echo = 2.0 x (1 + baseContributionPerEcho 0.02) = 2.04 structure-fractions/hour. Leaving the knob at 2.0 would give a full 6-Echo roster 6 x 2.04 = 12.24/h, a silent 6x buff. Anchoring the FULL roster at parity gives 2.04 / 6 = 0.34; rounded to 0.35 the 6-Echo aggregate is 6 x 0.35 x 1.02 = 2.14/h (+5% vs the old felt rate). Early game is intentionally slower per-Echo (1 Echo = 0.357/h) because passive repair is now FREE -- it no longer costs the Echo its harvest assignment, so the per-Echo rate had to come down. OWNER: this is the tuning dial -- raise it if mending feels too slow to notice; each +0.1 adds ~0.61/h at a full roster. Repair still SPENDS materials (F8-42 canon), so the knob only sets pace, never cost. Keep EchoBalanceData.RepairFractionPerHour's code default in step with this value. WO-1474 (2026-09-06): harvestRatePerHour was ADDED -- the three workforce rates (common 3600 / gold 900 / crystals 4) were private consts in EchoBonusCalculator.cs and therefore out of reach of the WO-1331 remote seam; they are authored here at the SAME values, so the move alone changes no number. In the same pass perEchoBaseRate finally became LIVE: HarvestTargetWeights now multiplies each Echo's per-hour rate by BaseRateFor(id) -- it resolved the roster entry and then discarded it before today -- so the sentence above about perEchoBaseRate doubling as the DumpSilos split weight is now TRUE rather than aspirational. EFFECT ON THE LIVE SPLIT at an all-matched roster: Wood x1.1 (echo-verdant-stag), Iron x1.15 (echo-stonewarden-bear), Crystals x0.45 (echo-ember-phoenix); Food and both Gold Echoes are authored at 1.0 and do not move. STALE ABOVE: the 'Bran+Maren (0.45 each) are the two Crystals harvesters' sentence does not match the authored rows -- only echo-ember-phoenix is 0.45, and echo-stormcoil-serpent is a GOLD Echo at 1.0.",

WHY 1.1: measured from enemies.json (19 rows, 2026-08-26) gold base is min 3 / median 18 / mean 31.1 / max 120; 1.1 puts the MEDIAN enemy (troll-mage, gold 18) at 20 -- the ruled number -- while preserving scale-with-difficulty. A FLAT 20 was considered and REJECTED: it makes farming the weakest enemy optimal. A 0.25 constant was discussed earlier and is SUPERSEDED (it was agreed on a misread of per-WAVE vs per-KILL and pays ~10x under intent). WHY FLOOR 6: cellar-hollow (gold 3) would otherwise pay 3 and a kill that pays almost nothing reads as broken. WHY CAP 40: uncapped, a necromancer (gold 120) pays 132 of EVERY material, so one boss out-earns a whole wave and the felt curve inverts. STONE: the Stone the HUD shows is Resources.Food / EconomyService.Food (DEF-121 repurposed the retired Stone axis). The grant goes through EconomyService like wood and iron. GameState.Stone is a second, phantom balance shown nowhere and spent by nothing -- NEVER route a reward there (WO-1212). GOLD is NOT listed here: it keeps its existing WO-432/433 grant unchanged and is the reference the other three derive from -- do not add a gold multiplier or it double-pays. perMaterialMultiplier is the per-resource override seam: 1.0 = the shared constant. "impulsePacks": "Packs 14-25 (tiers 14-25) are the WO-1037 SINGLE-RESOURCE IMPULSE PACKS, authored 2026-08-17 under the owner ruling of 2026-08-16 (option (b), verbatim: \"we should have small instant packs\" / \"small wood only\") and legalised by the WO-947 s12 amendment (the PURCHASE boundary is not the COST boundary). ONE family per harvestable resource (wood, iron, stone, crystals) x small/medium/large. THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: each of these SKUs carries EXACTLY ONE economy key and an EMPTY cosmetics + convenience list. A multi-resource impulse bundle would re-mix the WO-947 cost baskets through the back door and is FORBIDDEN (WO-947 s12c guardrail 1) - asserted headlessly by DeNelle.Editor.Regression.ImpulsePackRegression [impulse-pack], which also pins the $5 PRICE CEILING (owner standing ruling, memory solana-store-early-access-pack-pricing) and the no-structures/no-levels/no-queue-completions rule. AMOUNTS ARE PENDING OWNER RATIFICATION - they were sized against the REAL demand curve read out of building-tiers.json (tier costWood 500..16000, costFood 300..13000, costCrystal 100..4800) and structures-catalog.json (repo.upgradeCost iron 20..1440): small closes the cheapest tier upgrade (the Lumber Mill T1 900-wood shortfall in the screenshot that prompted this WO), medium closes a mid-ladder step, large closes a late step but deliberately NOT the Barracks T6 16000-wood ceiling, so the top pack does not trivialise the game. "raidCooldownSeconds": "WO-1379 (owner ruling 2026-09-04, landed at the door 2026-09-05): RETIRED AS A GATE - Heartfire (HeartfireService, one global charge pool) is the ONE gate on WHEN you may raid; the raid door (RaidSelectionScreen.OnCardTapped) no longer refuses on this window and the raid card no longer paints Recovering. The field is RETAINED, not deleted and not retuned: RaidCooldownService.BeginAfterClear still stamps the recovery RECORD from it on every clear (save evidence - SaveMigrator v41 derives everCompletedRaid from that record), and every camp row carries _raidCooldownSecondsSuperseded. Everything after this sentence describes the window AS IT WAS BUILT; read UN-RAIDABLE as recorded-as-recovering. ORIGINAL NOTE: WO-728 / owner ruling 2026-08-21, rationale corrected by WO-1134 - seconds this camp stays UN-RAIDABLE after a clear. Regular 14400 (4h) / Hard 28800 (8h) / Extreme 43200 (12h). 0 or absent falls back to the identical difficulty table in RaidCooldownService. THIS IS A PACING KNOB. It is NO LONGER THE CRYSTAL BOUND - THE UTC DAY IS. This entry used to say 'THIS NUMBER IS THE CRYSTAL BOUND, NOT A PACING KNOB' and '12h = ~2 clears/day = ~242 crystals/day'; both are now wrong, the second by 2x. Under the WO-1134 daily ruling a camp pays crystals on the FIRST clear of each UTC day ONLY (RaidClaimService.CrystalsPaidToday); further clears the same day pay reduced ORDINARY resources and ZERO crystals, so an Extreme camp pays 121 crystals/day, not ~242, and this window now bounds only within-day repeats that pay no crystals anyway. Crystals are still the one unbounded faucet in principle (RaidScoring.ComputeLoot pays FOOD and CRYSTALS ONLY - zero wood, zero iron - so the raid loop cannot fund its own troop costs); the day stamp is what bounds them now, and the day stamp is the lever to retune, NOT these hours. The 12h number itself is UNCHANGED and still an owner ruling. Crystals buy instant-finish, so SHORTENING these still defunds the timer ladder the game is paced by. Do not retune from how a single play session feels; a play session is not a day. The window is measured on the SERVER-ANCHORED clock (TimeSource), never the device clock.",

THE OWNER'S DISTINCTION, recorded so nobody re-litigates it: the jeweler SELLS things that happen to be precious; the Cathedral is WHERE MAGIC UPGRADES LIVE AND WHERE NEW SPELL TIERS UNLOCK  -  it is the ENGINE of magical progression, not a vendor that deals in it. 'behaviorId: GameplayBuilding' describes its BEHAVIOUR (it is not a firing tower), NOT its cost class. The surface evidence genuinely points both ways, so the ruling is the tiebreak  -  do not re-classify it off the id, the behaviorId or the _heightNote. Do not resurrect the row. MagicalIds therefore holds THREE ids at v20: 'tower_arcane_spire', 'healing_caravan', 'arcane-tower'.",

"notes": "Build-mode structure catalog  -  DATA-DRIVEN. Add a row here (+ keep the Resources/Data/Canonical copy byte-equal) and it flows into CatalogRegistry at startup via CatalogBootstrap. 'type' / 'mustSitOn' / 'navSurface' / 'element' are enum NAMES (StringEnumConverter). 'visualPrefabPath' is a Resources-relative path (LogWarning-safe on miss per CLAUDE.md §4). 'behaviorId' is resolved to a Village component by StructureFactory.AttachBehavior  -  only DefenseTower / WallSegment / CrystalMine / Gate are wired; null = inert decoration. S4: 'repo.cost' is the multi-resource build cost (wood/food/iron/crystals); it is charged + refunded through the persisted ResourceLedger (EconomyService). When 'cost' is omitted / all-zero, placement falls back to charging 'buildCost' Crystals (back-compat). S5 (the CoC upgrade sink): 'repo.maxLevel' (default 1 = not upgradeable; ceiling = RepoProps.MaxStructureLevel, raised 3 -> 6 by WO-966 for the storage containers; the StructureTierVisual accent ladder still tops out at 3, which is cosmetic only) is the highest level the UPGRADE verb can reach; 'repo.upgradeCost' is an optional per-step multi-resource table indexed by the level being upgraded TO minus 2 (entry [0] = L1->L2, [1] = L2->L3, ... [4] = L5->L6). When 'upgradeCost' is omitted, the upgrade cost falls back to the build 'cost' scaled by the level being left (L1->L2 = 1x, L2->L3 = 2x) -- a fallback that goes badly wrong on a long ladder, which is why the six-level containers author the table explicitly. StructureTierVisual steps the look (scale + bronze/silver/gold accent); DefenseTower range/damage and WallSegment toughness step the stats. v5 (StructureSingleton v2, owner only-ever-one ruling): 'repo.bakedTwins' lists the legacy baked scene-root GameObject names that REPRESENT a singleton row (twin standdown/resurface + IsBuilt, enforced generically by StructureSingleton with zero per-row code); null/absent = none; only meaningful with 'repo.singleton': true.",
